title: This Deer Is the Size of a Cat, and It Escapes Predators by Hiding Underwater

scenes.text: A deer the size of a cat. When it's hunted, it vanishes underwater.
Mouse-deer, or chevrotains, weigh as little as four pounds. No species is bigger than a small dog.
In 2008, researchers in Borneo watched one dive into a forest stream. It stayed under for more than five minutes at a time.
It surfaced four or five times in an hour, then went down again. Underwater, mouse-deer crouch and walk along the bottom.
In Sri Lanka, another one dove into a pond to escape a mongoose. The mongoose gave up after fifteen minutes. The deer didn't.
Whales evolved from small hoofed animals that took to the water. This cat-sized deer may be showing us how it started.

description:
Mouse-deer, among the smallest hoofed mammals at 4 to 33 pounds, escape predators by diving into streams and ponds and hiding underwater.
A 2010 paper in Mammalian Biology (Meijaard and colleagues) described a greater mouse-deer in Borneo staying submerged for more than five minutes at a time, surfacing only four or five times in an hour, and a Sri Lankan mouse-deer diving repeatedly to escape a mongoose; water chevrotains walk along the river bottom and hold their breath for about four minutes. The authors suggest this ancient escape trick is a clue to how the ancestors of whales first moved into water.
What is the strangest escape trick you know in nature?
subject: mouse deer
first_comment: Male mouse-deer have no antlers; they grow two long fangs instead and stab rivals with them. Which animal would you never expect to see swimming?
